summary: Missouri Conservation Commission fire tower near Richwoods: land bought 1939, built 1940-43, towerman 1950, upkeep logged to 1982. No source describes the site today.

events.note: Conservation Commission acquires ten acres for a fire tower site
CCC Company 2728 prepares the tower site and trail; the plan copies the Meramec Park and Leasburg towers
The 1942 annual report lists one pole tower, a garage and a woodshed as that year's construction. The 1939-41 order was for a 68-foot steel tower, so the tower type is unresolved
District forester reports building the cabin at the tower
Tracy Stoddard and family move to the tower; he is to be the towerman
Tower replacement recorded in the fiscal year 1953-54 report
Major repairs to the tower residence (fiscal year 1967-68)
New deep well pump and pump house installed at the towersite (fiscal year 1969-70)
Tower rewired and a new heater installed (fiscal year 1971-72)
Front porch and a bathroom floor in the residence replaced (fiscal year 1981-82); the last entry on the page

evidence.supports: Ten acres acquired by the Conservation Commission for a fire tower, 1939
evidence.quote: Ten acres were acquired by the Conservation Commission for the purpose of erecting a fire tower.

evidence.supports: Material for a 68-foot steel tower ordered, 1939-41
evidence.quote: Material for a 68-foot steel tower ordered.

evidence.supports: Site on the highest hill, known as High Pointe, ten miles south of Richwoods
evidence.quote: The tower site is ten miles south of Richwoods, Mo., on the highest hill in that vicinity, known as High Pointe.

evidence.supports: Washington County, Missouri Conservation Commission as agency
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Washington County - Missouri Conservation Commission - 39N-1E-35

evidence.supports: CCC Company 2728 preparing the ground for the tower and towerman's cottage, July 1940

William Towell, District Forester, with offices in Sullivan is supervising the construction.

evidence.supports: 1942 construction: one pole tower, garage and woodshed
evidence.quote: Construction and development during 1942: 1 pole tower, 1 garage and woodshed.

evidence.quote: Tower replacement was made at High Point in Washington County.

A new well was drilled at High Point towersite.

evidence.quote: A new deep well pump and pump house were installed at High Point towersite.

evidence.supports: Tower rewired and new heater, fiscal 1971-72

corrections.why: 20.7 m (68 ft) matches the 68-foot steel tower ordered in 1939-41, not a built height. The 1942 annual report lists a pole tower, and no source gives the height of the structure that was built.

notes_for_editor: All facts come from one hobbyist transcription (Central US Lookouts) of Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports and 1940-1950 newspaper items. I did not open the originals (the annual reports, the St. Clair Chronicle, the Sullivan News, the Daily Capital News). Tower type is unresolved: the 1939-41 entry orders a 68-foot steel tower, and the 1942 report lists a pole tower; the story says so and does not choose. The record's height_m (20.7 m) is a correction candidate for that reason. Direction from Richwoods differs slightly (south in 1940, southwest in 1943). The page's last entry is fiscal 1981-82, so current status, ownership and access are unknown and are left out of facts. The WebSearch budget ran out after my first search for this site; I did not run a second search or any workaround. The MDC article 'Shooting the Smoke' says MDC still had about 50 fire towers, but does not name High Point, so it is not cited here. A search-enabled rerun should check whether the tower still stands and whether the site is open.
